Write a plan to a file

Source: R/write-to.R
write_to.Rd

write_to() is the terminal verb that sends a plan to any format in GDAL's suite rather than into R. The driver comes from the file extension unless you name one.

Usage

write_to(x, dsn, ...)

Arguments

x

A source from src(), usually after query().

dsn

Where to write it.

...

The named arguments below.

Value

dsn, invisibly.

Details

A warped plan compiles straight into GDAL's own reprojection pipeline and never enters R at all, which is what you want for a large result. Every other plan is read into memory and written back out, because the read and the write are each one call and the intermediate is the size of the result you asked for rather than the size of the source. If that intermediate is too big, narrow the plan with dim first, or tile it yourself.

Arguments

driver

The GDAL driver's short name. The default reads it from the extension of dsn.

options

Character vector of "KEY=VALUE" creation options, such as c("COMPRESS=ZSTD", "TILED=YES").

layer

Vector only. The layer name to create. Defaults to the file's base name.

geometry_name, fid_name

Vector only. What the written layer calls its geometry and its feature id. NULL, the default, leaves it to the driver, which is geom and fid for a GeoPackage. Only a format that stores them as named columns can take a name (GeoPackage, SQLite, PostgreSQL, Parquet); a shapefile or GeoJSON has nowhere to put one, and GDAL warns and ignores it.

Examples

x <- src(system.file("extdata/test.tif", package = "GDAL7"))
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".tif")
write_to(query(x, dim = c(10, 5)), path)
src(path)
#> raster source GTiff  10 x 5 x 2
#>   extent -180, 180, -90, 90
#>   crs    EPSG:4326
#>   nothing missing
unlink(path)
